SUBJECT
: COVID-19 Preparedness Measures for Rainy Season
I.
RATIONALE
With the on-going disaster response operations for COVID-19 pandemic, the
National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) member
agencies and partner stakeholders prepare for this year’s rainy season. As a result of
COVID-19, the country is facing unprecedented challenges as we respond to recurring
hazards such as tropical cyclones, earthquake and volcanic eruption. COVID-19 does
not stop other disasters from happening but the pandemic leads us to shift and adjust
on how to prepare for them. The NDRRMC has been making efforts to not just continue
regular operations for disasters but to anticipate to the appropriate preparedness
measures while COVID-19 response continues.
This policy issuance is being issued to provide actionable guidance to the
NDRRMC member agencies and Response Clusters, Regional, Local DRRM Councils
and Barangay DRRM Committees, Non-Government Organizations, Private Sector
and the general public to prepare for response operations for the rainy season in
adherence to the public health measures amidst the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.
This document focuses on the rainy season but can also be applied to other non-
COVID-19 related incidents.
ll.
REFERENCES
A. The National Disaster Response Plan (NDRP) still serves as the national
government's strategic action in providing response assistance for managing
the consequences
of hazards and
its
potential
risks. The NDRP
will be

operations is in adherence to the implementation of the National Action Plan led
by the National Task Force.

B. The Operation Listo remain in effect as the institutionalized and standardized
local protocol and platform for early preparedness, response, and monitoring

C. The DOH Guidelines on Risk Based Public Health Standards for COVID-19
Mitigation is strictly integrated in this policy as a guidance for planning on the
implementation of Non-Pharmaceutical Interventions (NPIs) as minimum public
health standards to mitigate the threat of COVID-19.
D. The DBM Local Budget Circular on Policy Guidelines on the Provision pf
Funds By Local Government Units For Programs, Projects, And Activities To
Address The Corona Virus Disease 2019 (Covid-19) Situation is integrated to
guide the LGUs in providing necessary funds for COVID-19-related programs,
projects, and activities.
lll.
| GENERAL MEASURES ON RAINY SEASON PREPAREDNESS
A. NDRRMC member Agencies and Response Clusters
The member agencies of the NDRRMC and the Response Clusters are advised
to undertake the following preparedness measures:
Risk-informed decision making. The science and warning agencies shall provide
scientific data on the imminent risks in the country. The DOH shall also provide data
on the demographic profile of low to high risks to COVID-19 areas which will serve
as a main reference for decision making.
COVID-19 Response Operations. The operationalization of the National Action
Plan for COVID-19 activated the NDRRMC as the National Task Force in which the
functions of the Response Clusters are harmonized to the said plan, serving as
Task Groups, Sub-Task Groups and Task Units of the National Incident Command.
The member agencies are advised to operate and harmonize functions in the
NDRRMC Response Cluster.
Other Response Operations. In anticipation to the impacts of natural and human-
induced hazards that may happen during the COVID-19 response operations, the
NDRRMC will activate the NDRP aligned to the Inter-Agency Task Force for
Emerging Infectious Diseases (IATF- EID) Resolutions and Guidelines, and the
DOH Guidelines on Risk Based Public Health Standards for COVID-19.
All other
regular functions of the NDRRMC during response operations will be maintained
but with strict adherence to all these policy issuances.
Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment and other related meetings will be conducted
through an on-line platform.
Response Clusters. The respective response clusters are advised to undertake
inventory of resources including human resource, checking of vital
facilities,
stockpiling of food and non-food items and other essential logistical requirements
in preparation for the rainy season.

Situation Reporting. The COVID-19 report shall remain under the NTF through
the NIC while the national situation reports for other disasters such as for tropical
cyclone, earthquake etc. shall be consolidated by the NDRRMC through the OCD.
Duty at the Emergency Operations Center. The NDRRM EOC personnel and
staff will
strictly observe safety and health protocols during the tour of duty.
Response Cluster duty personnel will report to the NDRRM EOC as directed by the
lead clusters. However, COVID-19 mitigation measures will be implemented at all
times through practice of physical distancing, checking of body temperature and
wearing of face masks.
B. Local Government Unit and Local DRRM Offices
To assist our Local Chief Executives, DRRM Officers and health officials, the

harmonizing key concepts on the Operation Listo Manual and the DOH Guidelines on
Risk Based Public Health Standards for COVID-19 Mitigation. The following are the
essential guidelines for preparedness planning of LGUs:
Science and evidence-based decision through conduct of Pre-Disaster Risk
Assessment (PDRA). The PAGASA, MGB, DOH and other warning agencies shall
be consulted for the imminent risks in the LGU. Undertake the minimum measures
as stated in the Oplan Listo such as activation of Emergency Operations Center,
Incident Management Team, budget and logistical requirements for the response.
Vital facilities and services. The LGU is advised to anticipate and prepare for the
impacts of the rainy season to vital facilities such as hospitals and clinics, local
government offices, power and water services and ensure proper checking and
retrofitting of facilities.
Local DRRM Funding. Through the Bayanihan to Heal As One Act, the thirty
percent (30%) cap on the amount appropriated for the Quick Response Fund is
lifted. LGUs are authorized to utilize the LDRRMF beyond the 30% QRF to address
the disaster response requirements of the COVID-19 emergency provided that the
same
is consistent with the approved LDRRMP as incorporated
in the Annual
Investment Program. This means the LGUs are authorized to realign preparedness
fund or the 70% of the Local DRRM Fund to support the programs, activities and
projects for disaster response.
Logistics Requirements for rainy season. LGUs are advised to increase capability
to stockpile food and non-food items for rainy season response operations.
Evacuation Planning. With the respective LGU evacuation plans, assess and
review community demographics and identify areas facing low, moderate and high
risk from COVID-19 and ensure observance to physical distancing (at least
1 meter
apart) in evacuation centers. Provide due priority to vulnerable citizens such as
elderly, pregnant women, children, persons with disabilities and individuals with
underlying conditions.

Inventory of evacuation centers not listed as quarantine facilities. These facilities
must be prepared in case of evacuation and must adhere to the guidelines on
physical distancing to reduce transmission and contact of COVID-19.
Operations as Local Task Force COVID-19. The LDRRMCs are advised to
explore incident management options suited for the on-going COVID-19 response
operations and the anticipation for the rainy season.
Safety of Responders. Use of PPE and other protective apparel must be observed
in the response operations to ensure safety. Other health procedures include,
temperature and health screening prior to entry at all facilities or sites, wearing of
face masks and cleaning and disinfection of facilities.
Social Services. Distribution of relief goods and management of evacuation
centers must observe COVID-19 mitigation measures. Mass gatherings are strictly
prohibited. LGUs are advised to designate distribution areas with appropriate safety
markings.
C. General Public
The general public is also advised to undertake measures in preparation to the rainy
season during COVID-19 response and to support the efforts of the LGU. The following
are the key steps:
Monitor the news for weather updates, warning and advisories. Coordinate
with local authorities for the preparedness measures for the rainy season.
Check your Go bag. Prepare for your family’s go bag containing items such as
food packs, clothes, whistle, flashlight, medicine, radio and etc.
Practice respiratory etiquette at all times. Use of tissue or the inner portion of
the elbow to cover the nose and mouth when sneezing/ coughing. Practice proper
disposal of tissue after use.
Wear Face mask. Use cloth face mask for general public and surgical mask/
medical-grade mask for individuals with flu-like symptoms and with other underlying
conditions.
Practice Physical distancing with at least 1 meter apart.
Stay at home.
Elderly,
individuals with
underlying
conditions,
persons with
disabilities, children and pregnant women must stay at home and limit their travel.
If there’s a need for preemptive evacuation, limit the exposure and contact to other
individuals
by

physical

and

Coordinate with LGUs for proper housing in the evacuation centers.
Stockpile Relief Goods at home. Meanwhile, LGUs will designate areas for
distribution of relief goods and individuals are ask to follow safety protocols set by
the LGUs.

Sanitation. Conduct disinfection of frequently touched surfaces such as but not
limited to tables, doorknobs,
light switches, phones, toilets and among others
using .5% bleach solution.
D. NGOs, CSOs, Private Sector and Other Partner Stakeholders
Partner stakeholders of the NDRRMC are encouraged to coordinate with LGUs in
the prepositioning of resources and other preparedness activities. The deployment of
teams shall be made in accordance to the LGU incident management protocols and in
adherence to public health measures.
As the country anticipates for the rainy season, NDRRMC’s main priorities are to
ensure life safety, to provide life sustainment to emergencies and incidents, and to
continue the delivery of government services amidst the complex disasters. The
NDRRMC enjoins the LGU, DRRM Officers, health officials, Private Sector, NGOs,
CSOs and the general public to continue with our disaster preparedness measures for
rainy season while embracing the new normal brought by the COVID-19 pandemic.
The rainy season preparedness efforts are adjusted as we practice physical distancing
and wearing of face masks to reduce contact and exposure to individuals. The
NDRRMC
will continue to operate with a whole-of-society-approach for disaster
preparedness and response to the highest level possible.
